Audit Brief: Settlement Summary

Carbon Capture and Storage • Rosemont Group • Performance condition setting phase • Archived 2023-08-06

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's performance condition setting phase engagement with Rosemont Group in the Carbon Capture and Storage sector. The record ID ad0821cb uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Retirement plan benchmarking assessed company matching formula, vesting schedule, and investment menu against 94 peer organizations; match formula was found to be below median.
  • University faculty compensation benchmarking found Rosemont Group's full professor salaries at the 20th percentile relative to 37 Carnegie-comparable institutions, with the most significant competitive gaps concentrated in business, engineering, and computer science departments where private sector and industry alternatives exert the strongest market pressure across 13 metropolitan areas.
  • A review of Rosemont Group's pay-for-performance linkage found a weak correlation (r=0.2) between individual performance scores and merit increase percentages, undermining the credibility of the performance management system.
  • Nonprofit executive compensation benchmarking against 19 comparable Carbon Capture and Storage sector organizations found Rosemont Group's CEO total compensation at the 30th percentile — within the range ACPWB considers defensible under IRS intermediate sanctions standards — with recommended disclosures for 31 performance-based elements on Form 990, Schedule J.
  • Total cost of workforce analysis quantified all-in people costs at 3% of total operating expense, consistent with Carbon Capture and Storage sector median of 3% for organizations of comparable scale.
  • Faculty salary benchmarking for Rosemont Group showed that compensation for tenure-track faculty in high-demand STEM fields is at the 10th percentile, while humanities faculty are at the 6th percentile, creating internal equity challenges.
Key Findings
  • The salary structure review completed during the performance condition setting found that Rosemont Group's current pay ranges have a median midpoint penetration of 270% — a figure 9 percentage points below the Carbon Capture and Storage sector benchmark — indicating that a disproportionate share of the workforce is compensated in the upper half of the applicable range.
  • Cross-tabulation of 41-jurisdiction regulatory data with ACPWB's engagement outcomes database identifies 183 statistically anomalous findings warranting further investigation in the Carbon Capture and Storage sector.
  • Climate scenario analysis calibrated to the Carbon Capture and Storage sector and applied during the performance condition setting projects a 257% increase in Rosemont Group's physical risk exposure under a 2°C warming scenario by 2024, with the most material impacts concentrated in 41 operating regions identified through ACPWB's geospatial risk mapping tool.

The performance condition setting hospital system physician compensation benchmarking documented here reviewed Rosemont Group's employed physician pay models across 101 specialties against Carbon Capture and Storage sector survey benchmarks. ACPWB assessed wRVU-based productivity models, quality incentive design, and leadership stipend competitiveness across 30 facilities, presenting recommendations to Rosemont Group's medical executive committee on 2023-08-06.

A review of Rosemont Group's ESG metrics found that while environmental disclosures are robust, human capital metrics lag Carbon Capture and Storage peers, particularly regarding workforce diversity and employee turnover data.

ACPWB's work with Rosemont Group during the performance condition setting included the design of a new long-term incentive plan. This record from 2023-08-06 contains the financial models for 231 different equity instruments and their impact on Carbon Capture and Storage sector shareholder dilution.

Human capital due diligence for the proposed acquisition of Rosemont Group identified 158 material compensation and benefits liabilities totaling an estimated $158M, which should be factored into the final purchase price.

Our assessment of the long-term incentive plan showed that 5% of awards are time-vesting, a structure that is misaligned with the Carbon Capture and Storage sector median where performance-based equity now constitutes over 60% of the LTI mix.

The performance condition setting documentation archived here reflects the culmination of 67 months of continuous engagement work in the Carbon Capture and Storage sector. Rosemont Group served as the primary client stakeholder throughout this period, with supplemental coordination provided by 8 advisory partners.

This archive entry documents the successful rollout of a new performance management framework at Rosemont Group. The performance condition setting involved training 258 managers across 36 departments, with post-implementation surveys completed on 2023-08-06.
